name: Grain ferment extract
lead: Grain ferment extract is a skincare ingredient name used for extracts made by fermenting cereal grains such as rice, barley or wheat with yeast or bacteria and then filtering or processing the result. Products that list it, typically as a named grain plus "ferment extract" or "ferment filtrate" in the ingredient list, are used in toners, essences, serums and moisturisers, where people use them as part of a routine aimed at smoother, more hydrated-looking, more even-toned skin.[1]

Fermentation is the long-established process in which yeasts or bacteria convert carbohydrates in a food or grain into alcohol or organic acids; grain ferments in food include sake, beer, kvass, sourdough and rice-and-lentil batters.[1] Cosmetic grain ferments borrow the same idea, applying a fermented liquid to the skin rather than eating or drinking it. The best-known example is the sake-derived yeast ferment: SK-II's story, as recounted on Wikipedia, is that Japanese scientists in the 1970s noticed elderly sake brewery workers had smooth, clear, young-looking hands, and a yeast extract the company calls Pitera was later isolated for cosmetic use.[2]

A related ingredient, Galactomyces ferment filtrate, described as a by-product of sake fermentation, is used as a moisturising agent with antioxidant effects that is said to improve the skin's moisture barrier.[3] The ingredient is not a single defined compound: the contents depend on the grain, the microbe and the process, and brands describe them in their own terms.

chain: Fermented grain liquid is included in a toner, essence or serum
Applied to the face as part of a daily routine
Skin that people describe as softer, brighter and more hydrated-looking
angle.text: People use products containing grain ferment extract in the toner or essence step of a skincare routine, aiming for smoother, more luminous-looking skin. Brands describe the ingredient as hydrating and brightening; a small study of a 97% filtrate essence reported fewer enlarged pores and blackheads and less sebum.

paras: A grain ferment extract is made by fermenting a cereal grain or its extract with yeast or bacteria, then filtering or otherwise processing the liquid for use in cosmetics. Fermentation in general is the conversion of carbohydrates by microorganisms into alcohol or organic acids.[1] Ingredient lists name the grain and the word ferment, for example a rice, barley or wheat ferment extract or filtrate.

SK-II was developed in the 1970s in Japan after scientists observed that elderly workers at a sake brewery had smooth, young-looking hands from long contact with fermenting yeast; the brand launched in the early 1980s and uses a yeast extract it calls Pitera.[2] Wikipedia's SK-II article cites no clinical studies of Pitera and records a 2005 controversy in China in which Procter & Gamble paid a fine after a customer alleged inaccurate advertising and an allergic reaction.[2]

The ingredient is most often found in leave-on products such as toners, essences and serums used on the face. Proponents and brands associate it with hydration, a brighter complexion and softer skin texture. The exact composition varies between products, since the grain, microorganism and process differ.
As with other plant-derived cosmetic ingredients, people with grain allergies or sensitivities may react to products containing grain extracts; label ingredient lists show which grain is used.

Wikipedia's Galactomyces article describes a study of 20 volunteers who used an essence containing 97% Galactomyces ferment filtrate. Compared with untreated control faces, enlarged pores and blackheads decreased by more than 15.66% and 21.84% respectively, and sebum fell by 64.17%; the authors concluded the essence had a beneficial effect on facial skin.[3] No trial of a rice, barley or wheat ferment extract as a standalone ingredient was found.

timeline.event: Japanese scientists link sake brewery workers' smooth hands to fermenting yeast, leading to SK-II.[2]
Controversy in China over SK-II advertising and an alleged allergic reaction.[2]

card.summary: A fermented-cereal skincare ingredient used in toners and essences for smoother, more hydrated-looking skin.
card.aka: Rice ferment, barley ferment, wheat ferment filtrate
card.note: People with grain allergies may react to grain-derived ingredients.

quick.overview:
Grain ferment extract is an ingredient in skincare made by fermenting grains like rice or barley and using the resulting liquid in toners, essences and serums.

People use it in the hydrating steps of a routine for softer, brighter-looking skin. It is a category of ingredient rather than one defined compound, so products vary.
quick.mechanism: Yeasts or bacteria ferment the grain's carbohydrates; the filtered liquid is added to a formula and applied to the skin like any leave-on product.
quick.risks: Generally sold as an ordinary cosmetic ingredient. Allergy to the source grain is the main stated caveat.
